sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`import` and `migrate` both have `--dry-run`; `remove` does not. `remove --purge` is the
one destructive, non-obviously-reversible operation, and it surfaces its consequences —
a dependent left dangling, an id that stays burned because a commit cites it — only in a
*later* `slicer check`. A preview would turn a surprise into a decision.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `remove --purge --dry-run` reports what would be deleted and writes nothing.
2. It names any dependents and says whether the id would be freed.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `--dry-run` to `remove`. For purge, report the item, its dependents, and whether the
id would be reclaimed or stay burned (the same logic purge already computes), without
writing. Retire can share the flag.

**Not in this slice:** a general undo — git is the undo for a committed `.slicer/`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `remove --purge --dry-run` previews the deletion and its fallout.
